reasons: Full six-block model did not reliably meet total CPU and 200 ms processing screens on the shared target desktop
Serial High Quality cascade adds CPU and native algorithmic latency; worsens target-only SI-SDR versus extraction alone
Four-block four-frame extraction passed two full streams, but pinned ordinary-quiet runtime failed
Alternate enrolled voice in the compact variant only gains 0.5/3.8 dB selection; FP32 also weak, so INT8 is not the root cause
OpenVINO executes FP32 reference LSTM kernels even for imported dynamic-INT8 graph and does not meet runtime limits here
ORT 1.30 Python comparison does not establish a passing full-model screen
Weight redistribution terms, live worker/host timing, word preservation and real call quality remain unresolved
streaming_pipeline_continuation.machine: 12th Gen Intel Core i5-1235U; shared desktop with changing background CPU workloads
measurement_limits: This is offline source-release/deadline simulation with actual paced wall-clock measurements, not actual PipeWire worker latency
Most runs pinned CPU 2; two-thread runs CPUs 0 and 2; P-core pool runs CPUs 0-3; normal-scheduling runs retain all allowed CPUs
Initialization and synthetic prior excluded; final parent CPU accounting also includes paced waits; older chunk CPU sums exclude idle spinning
Initial two cascade runs used precomputed input downsampling; later source callbacks perform bounded downsampling during processing
Scores are projection/energy/SI-SDR screens, not word-intelligibility certification; calibration overlap and development-set caveats remain
Quiet speech under a louder competitor not acoustically accepted; runtime replay includes the entire public scenario
Earlier completion-time code hashes are explicitly labeled; later source snapshots identify captured bytes actually executed
No GPU device exposed by isolated OpenVINO SDK; no GPU or driver changes attempted
checks: Native INT8 engine asserted; no silent ONNX fallback

Finite correctly drained output at exact expected length
